title: MV RPG Maker MV Software Rendering - Tackling Memory Leaks

posts.author: EnergySpike
posts.body:
I wasn't sure where to put this, but I wanted to release this for
anyone who are encountering memory leak issues with their RPG Maker MV editor.
To put it simply, this is a launcher workaround that disables GPU/OpenGL acceleration for RPG Maker MV editor sessions to avoid editor memory climb/crashes.
I've been using it for a bit now, and my memory usage hasn't peaked above 500 MB for very large projects (testing with 40+ scripts, 200+ maps with many having 100 x 100+ tiles).
To use this, all you have to do is drop the cmd file into the folder where your RPGMV.exe lives. For Steam Users, the original Launch Options edit has been retired for recommendation, as it proved to be woefully unreliable. The only reliable option is to directly launch the cmd file in the attached zip folder after placing it in your folder with the RPGMV.exe file (RPG Maker MV Editor).
=========================================================
Important: You'll need to launch the CMD file as Administrator, as well. Without Administrator privileges, you'll still rack up an unbearably high memory usage, even if Task Manager can't see it.
Important #2: If you save your project around 20-40 times in 1 session, RESTART YOUR RPG MAKER MV EDITOR! I spotted a separate memory leak that my CMD file can't cover. It's tiny, but can easily add up, especially if you haven't used the 4GB Patch.
Note: I've included another CMD file (V2) that might help with curbing the Save-induced memory leak issue. I'm still testing this, so it's still my experimental version, but figured I'd share it, anyway. It'll also launch with an admin-privilege request to give it a little more QoL improvement.
=========================================================
There are a few notes and caveats:
- This is a launcher workaround, not a patch.
- It does not modify RPGMV.exe or project files.
- It may also affect playtest windows launched by the editor.
- CPU usage may increase on some systems.
- GPU-heavy plugins, WebGL/3D effects, lighting systems, or video playback should be tested separately.
- If your editor was already stable, this may not be necessary.
- This was testing for MV only. I don't have MZ, so I have no idea if this will work for that or anything else.
- This was also only tested with an NVidia GPU, as that's all I have. I have no idea what will happen if you have any other GPU.
As long as you have a decent computer, though, you shouldn't really notice any real impact on editor performance, or editor-launched play test performance.
This may not be an all-round fix, but for those who are struggling with frequent crashes from memory leaks, like me, this may be useful.
I also don't know if this was already made prior, so if it was, let me know. I did look for fixes, but nothing really addressed the memory leak, itself. I hope this helps.

posts.author: EnergySpike
posts.body:
I should note, this fix is primarily for the RPGMV editor. I didn't intend, or test, for use with an actual deployed game.
Working as is, this plugin should not drastically affect Test-Launched games from the Editor, itself, either. There might be a few things that you may notice, but for the most part, it doesn't disable GPU usage for the actual play-test for most plugins that rely on the GPU.

Any performance loss encountered will not affect the actual deployed game, though.
The only purpose for making this fix was strictly to stop the Editor from eating up all your Ram until it explodes.

posts.author: EnergySpike
posts.body:
Speedy Update: The Steam Launch Option is unreliable.
Only launch the workaround using the cmd file provided.
A little extra context: The Steam Launch Option that was originally recommended for Steam Users (noted in the original Read Me file) was unable to cover what the cmd file could. The Steam Launch Options allowed for Events to rack up virtual memory horrifyingly fast just by opening and closing an Event menu.
The attached cmd file did not have this issue and is, so far, proving to be the most reliable for me, and that's saying something because I love to abuse RPGMV. Nothing really gets my blood pumping like having to restore a corrupted, once-heavily-modified json file for the 500th time in a single week. /s
Another Edit:
Launch the CMD file as Administrator.
Another another edit: I often chew before I take a bite of food. If you still have the original zip file, and are dead-set on using Steam, you'll need to verify that you're ABSOLUTELY launching RPGMV from Steam with Administrator Privileges. I haven't been able to get steam to launch anything reliably in Administrator, even if Steam itself was launched with Admin rights.
I won't provide the Launch Options for steam again, due to it's unreliability. Last thing I want is to give someone hope and have their dreams crumble as their Animations.json file that they spent 6 months on without backing up gets corrupted from RPGMV crashing mid-save. Again.
Another another another edit: I made a second Important Note in my main post in this thread. Saving within the editor still adds a tiny memory hike that doesn't seem to go away. My CMD file cannot cover it. The memory leak is tiny, thankfully, but it can easily sneak up on you if you aren't aware of it.
If you save your project around 20-40 times, save again and restart your RPG Maker MV Editor.
I did add a new cmd launcher (V2) that might help with curbing the memory leak for saving the project multiple times. I'm still testing, so its better to treat it as experimental. That being said, so far, this experimental version is proving to be my most reliable one with all the abuse I'm trying to cause.

posts.author: EnergySpike
posts.body:
A quick update:
The V2 version of the CMD file I've provided does seem to work, however, while frequent saving no longer consumes as much memory over time, everything (changing maps, frequent saving, opening/closing events/database) does add a tiny bit to the overall memory usage, with the biggest consumer of memory usage happening when you open another project from the one that you launched with. Creating new, large maps also seems to spike the memory usage.
Thankfully, it's not NEARLY as bad as default MV, so you'll have a ton more breathing room than even just using the 4GB Patch alone. That being said, using the 4GB Patch alongside this workaround launcher should dramatically help if you suffer from frequent crashes due to memory issues.
If you use the V2 version, if you load another project, I would advise you restart your MV Editor so that the project you want to work on is first to load. I would also advise you save and restart if you "Create" a new, large map.
I'll work on making some more QoL improvements to the workaround launcher.
Sorry, some additional information: While I do note that there is a very tiny memory leak, the scale is dramatically reduced. For some context on this, I'm loading between two large projects, one that uses 40+ plugins, several different tilesets, has several large maps, and tons of events that I'm sifting through, and another project that has maxed out map sizes (256x256) and actively working on with frequent event creations and saves, all in the same session. So far, my memory usage has been around 1.3GB after all of that, all within the same session. It's still within working boundaries, even if the 4GB patch wasn't applied (although I might get nervous if the 4GB Patch wasn't added, for my specific case).
